question: Under Colorado law, when a broker renews a three-year license and did not simply pass the Colorado portion of the real estate exam within the previous three years, how many total hours of continuing education credit must the broker complete, and how many of those hours must be Commission-developed credits?
choice_a: 24 total hours, 12 of which must be Commission-developed credits
choice_b: 24 total hours, 8 of which must be Commission-developed credits
choice_c: 12 total hours, 6 of which must be Commission-developed credits
choice_d: 24 total hours, all of which must be Commission-developed credits
explanation: Section 12-10-213(1)(a) requires a minimum of twenty-four hours of credit for a three-year license, twelve of which must be the credits developed by the commission under subsection (2).

question: A broker holds a license that expires less than three years after it was issued (the Transition Period licensing cycle) and did not pass the Colorado portion of the exam within the license period. Under 12-10-213(1)(b), what is the minimum number of Commission-developed credit hours required out of the 24-hour total?
explanation: Section 12-10-213(1)(b) requires a minimum of twenty-four hours of credit, at least eight of which must be the credits developed by the commission pursuant to subsection (2).

question: The Commission is required to develop twelve hours of credit designed to assure reasonable currency of real estate knowledge. Per 12-10-213(2), what must these credits include?
choice_a: A review of national real estate market trends
choice_b: Instruction in real estate appraisal techniques
choice_c: An update of the current statutes and the rules promulgated by the commission that affect the practice of real estate
choice_d: A survey of local multiple listing service procedures
explanation: Subsection (2) states the commission's twelve hours of credit 'shall include an update of the current statutes and the rules promulgated by the commission that affect the practice of real estate.'

question: A broker takes a course under Rule 250 of the Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure that concerns real property law. According to 12-10-213(2), what is the effect on the broker's continuing education requirement?
choice_a: The course cannot be used toward continuing education because Rule 250 courses are only for attorneys
choice_b: The broker must also retake an equivalent Commission-approved course to receive any credit
choice_c: The course counts only if it is also separately approved as a Commission distance-learning offering
choice_d: The broker shall receive credit for the course toward fulfillment of the continuing education requirements
explanation: The statute states that if a licensee takes a Rule 250 course that concerns real property law, 'the licensee shall receive credit for the course toward the fulfillment of the licensee's continuing education requirements.'

question: Per 12-10-213(2), the Commission-developed twelve hours of update credit must be taken from which of the following sources?
choice_a: An accredited Colorado college or university, a Colorado community college, a Colorado private occupational school with a certificate of approval, or an educational institution/service described in section 23-64-104
choice_b: Any real estate brokerage licensed in Colorado
choice_c: Any nationally accredited online continuing education provider regardless of state
choice_d: Any elective course provider approved by the Commission under Rule 4.6
explanation: Subsection (2) specifies these credits must be taken from an accredited Colorado college or university, a Colorado community college, a Colorado private occupational school holding a certificate of approval, or an educational institution or service described in section 23-64-104.

question: A broker holds a license that expires on December 31 of the same year it was first issued. What does the text say about this broker's continuing education obligation upon renewal?
choice_a: The broker must complete the full 24-hour requirement like all other brokers
choice_b: The broker is not subject to the continuing education requirements set forth in subsection (1)
choice_c: The broker only needs the 12 hours of Commission-developed update credit
choice_d: The broker must complete the Broker Reactivation Course instead
explanation: Section 12-10-213(4) and Rule 4.1.B provide that a licensee applying for renewal of a license that expires December 31 of the year it was issued is not subject to the continuing education requirements of subsection (1).

question: Under Rule 4.2.A.1, a broker satisfies continuing education through the standard 12-hour Annual Commission Update path, completed as annual 4-hour increments developed by the Commission. What restriction applies to repeating a version of the Annual Commission Update?
choice_a: A broker may repeat the same version once per licensing cycle for extra credit
choice_b: A broker may repeat the same version as long as it is taken in a different calendar year
choice_c: A broker may not take the same version of the Annual Commission Update more than once
choice_d: A broker may repeat the same version if it is taught by a different instructor
explanation: Rule 4.2.A.1 states, 'A Broker may not take the same version of the Annual Commission Update more than once.'

question: During the Transition Period licensing cycle, a broker satisfies continuing education by completing two different versions of the Annual Commission Update for eight credit hours. Per Rule 4.2.A.2, how many additional elective hours must the broker complete to reach the 24-hour total requirement?
explanation: Rule 4.2.A.2 requires an additional sixteen credit hours of electives, which combined with the eight hours from two versions of the Annual Commission Update meets the total 24-hour requirement during the Transition Period.

question: A broker has been Inactive for an accumulated total of 30 months prior to seeking to activate the license to Active status and is unable to comply with the continuing education paths in Rule 4.2.A.1 or A.2. Under Rule 4.2.A.3.b, which option is available to this broker?
choice_b: The 12-hour Annual Commission Update only, with no electives
choice_c: A written petition to the Commission for a continuing education waiver
choice_d: The 72-hour prelicensing education requirement under Rules 2.1.A.2.b and c
explanation: Rule 4.2.A.3.b makes the 24-hour Broker Reactivation Course available to a broker who is Inactive or Expired for an accumulative period of up to thirty-six months and unable to comply with the continuing education requirement in subsections A.1. or A.2.

question: To successfully complete the Annual Commission Update, what score must a broker achieve on the written or on-line course examination developed by the Commission?
explanation: Rule 4.3.C requires each broker to complete the Annual Commission Update 'by achieving a passing score of seventy percent (70%) on a written or on-line course examination developed by the Commission.'

question: Per Rule 4.4.A.4, what is the minimum instructional-time standard for a continuing education course?
choice_a: At least 45 instructional minutes per one-hour increment
choice_b: At least 40 instructional minutes per one-hour increment
choice_c: At least 50 instructional minutes per one-hour increment
choice_d: A full 60 instructional minutes per one-hour increment, with no exceptions
explanation: Rule 4.4.A.4 requires the course to be at least one hour increment in length, 'containing at least fifty (50) instructional minutes per one (1) hour increment.'

question: Which of the following is explicitly listed in Rule 4.4.B.2 as a course type that will NOT qualify for continuing education credit?
choice_d: Examination preparation or exam technique courses
explanation: Rule 4.4.B.2.d lists examination preparation or exam technique courses as an ineligible topic, while ethics, agency, and brokerage administration and management are all listed as eligible topics under Rule 4.4.B.1.

question: Per Rule 4.5.A, what is the maximum number of continuing education credit hours a broker may earn in a single day?
explanation: Rule 4.5.A states, 'A maximum of eight (8) hours of credit may be earned per day.'
